pr.body:
## Summary This pull request introduces a new feature to manage calendar cache data, including the ability to view cache status and delete cached data. It also includes several supporting updates to repositories, APIs, and UI components. Below is a summary of the most important changes grouped by theme. ### New Feature: Calendar Cache Management * Added a `deleteCache` mutation to the TRPC `calendarsRouter`, enabling users to delete cached calendar data by credential ID. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsxR27-R33](diffhunk://#diff-9e053175cc6dfb5717313e0587a730fff132f9d3c1200204f0ce8dac53a19280R27-R33)`) * Introduced the `deleteCacheHandler` to handle cache deletion logic, including validation of user access to the specified credential. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.tsR1-R33](diffhunk://#diff-572888b8e0555167a5787847f29d5a46623eff170491acc0654e916f5b4afd18R1-R33)`) * Updated the `connectedCalendarsHandler` to enrich calendar data with cache status (`cacheUpdatedAt`) by querying the `CalendarCacheRepository`. (`[packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.tsR27-R39](diffhunk://#diff-3f6a556ad60f26d0162770fcd81b5bddeb6ab0437552ac792045c3cd2608d710R27-R39)`) ### UI Enhancements * Created a new `CredentialActionsDropdown` component to display cache status and provide options to delete cached data or disconnect integrations. (`[packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsxR1-R134](diffhunk://#diff-c78273434b95ab8276bb5eb24d9bc088b10af029388bdcd08cbe478f44269b31R1-R134)`) * Replaced the `DisconnectIntegration` component with `CredentialActionsDropdown` in the `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` UI, integrating the new cache management functionality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L5-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L70-L81)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-831b0874e07f01721f87926262c5c9674ff9d7443741dfb71ceb849656345b00L125-L135)`) ### Repository and Database Updates * Added a `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method to the `CalendarCacheRepository` and its mock implementation to fetch cache statuses for multiple credentials. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b36c72c0db751ba0cafe234dfa150817672869825333c22b074c4977a6135b8dR30-R32)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ceffbae9ef3da413495feac73a341672e77ffaf493cf67ada0b637ead80ded38R26-R30)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4cf8d3089fad7b6c8fe4172d8d42147f136b65baf30b726e57b9b10d179d4a99R172-R188)`) * Introduced a new `updateManyByCredentialId` method in the `SelectedCalendarRepository` to update multiple calendars by credential ID. (`[packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.tsR400-R406](diffhunk://#diff-ccb4eecfa701e5b0c7d6ba87dcc550cdf3700a63ee252849045611599ecb9273R400-R406)`) * Added an `updatedAt` column to the `CalendarCache` table in the database schema and Prisma model to track the last update timestamp. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f597bd98bbcfdcf4861ee7bf0c238e7dfe54b456ceb69b852aaf3979c4102cfR1-R8)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-56fa4d384ba6fb94b130e9eb42c5cad00734b025ebd6c197f76873469725ae87R1718)`) ### Localization and Strings * Added new localization strings for cache management actions, such as "Cache Status," "Delete cached data," and "Cache deleted successfully." (`[apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.jsonR3376-R3382](diffhunk://#diff-57de4b8e5231f1d699891d98b0381d56e9e24537b0ca5420d1fba4f0597370bcR3376-R3382)`) ### Miscellaneous * Updated `package.json` to replace `ts-node` with `npx tsx` for running the `dev:cron` script. (`[apps/web/package.jsonL11-R11](diffhunk://#diff-14b60f636e1a2b0061da57aaf231cb1ed15a5dc0c592425ed82e58fec95d42d8L11-R11)`) ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human **🔴 High Priority (5 items)** - [x] **Verify deleteCache tRPC mutation exists** - The component references `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache.useMutation()` but this mutation implementation is not visible in the PR changes. Check if this endpoint exists or needs to be created. - [x] **End-to-end testing with Google Calendar** - Install a Google Calendar integration and verify the credential-level dropdown appears, shows cache status, and deletion flow works correctly with confirmation dialog. - [x] **Test cache status display logic** - Verify that `cacheUpdatedAt` timestamps are correctly formatted and displayed only for Google Calendar credentials with actual cache data. - [x] **Confirm repository pattern correctness** - Test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` returns accurate data and the credential-to-cache mapping works properly in the UI. - [x] **Verify dropdown conditional rendering** - Ensure the dropdown only appears for Google Calendar credentials and handles edge cases (no cache, disabled integrations, etc.). **Recommended Test Plan:** 1. Connect a Google Calendar integration to trigger cache creation 2. Navigate to `/apps/installed/calendar` 3. Verify dropdown appears on Google Calendar credential with cache status and timestamp 4. Test "Delete cached data" action shows confirmation dialog 5. Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately 6. Test "Remove App" functionality still works correctly --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD UI["CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx
(New Component)"]:::major-edit Handler["connectedCalendars.handler.ts
(Updated tRPC Handler)"]:::major-edit RepoInterface["calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts
(Updated Interface)"]:::minor-edit RepoImpl["calendar-cache.repository.ts
(Updated Implementation)"]:::minor-edit RepoMock["calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts
(Updated Mock)"]:::minor-edit Translations["common.json
(Added Translation Keys)"]:::minor-edit UI -->|"Uses repository via tRPC"| Handler Handler -->|"Calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds"| RepoImpl RepoImpl -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface RepoMock -->|"Implements"| RepoInterface UI -->|"Uses translation keys"| Translations subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - **Session Details**: Requested by @zomars, implemented in Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/24545e0980df465995521419432a2a52 - **SelectedCalendar.updatedAt Usage**: Currently only updated in backend via Google webhook handler but not displayed in frontend. Frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache. Consider if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update should be removed. - **Import Path Resolution**: Had to fix UI component import paths during development - watch for potential module resolution issues in different environments. - **Testing Limitation**: Local testing was limited due to no installed calendar integrations - end-to-end verification with real Google Calendar data is essential.

raw_findings.body: tRPC surfaces this as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) rather than a proper NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN error code, which breaks correct client-side error handling/monitoring and misclassifies an expected authorization failure as a server bug.
raw_findings.evidence: throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");
raw_findings.failure_mode: tRPC wraps unclassified errors as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, obscuring the real cause
raw_findings.impact: tRPC surfaces this as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) rather than a proper NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN error code, which breaks correct client-side error handling/monitoring and misclassifies an expected authorization failure as a server bug.
raw_findings.root_cause: Handler throws a plain JS Error instead of a TRPCError with an appropriate error code
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Throw a `TRPCError` from `@trpc/server` with an appropriate code (e.g. `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`) instead of a plain `Error`.
raw_findings.title: deleteCacheHandler throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
raw_findings.trigger: A user attempts to delete cache for a credentialId they do not own (e.g. tampered request, stale UI state, or race with credential deletion), causing `credential` to be null.

raw_findings.body: If the parent's onSuccess callback does not itself invalidate/refetch the connectedCalendars query, the 'Cache Status'/'Last updated' timestamp shown in the dropdown remains stale after a successful cache deletion.
raw_findings.failure_mode: UI continues to display the pre-deletion cache timestamp until an unrelated refetch occurs
raw_findings.impact: If the parent's onSuccess callback does not itself invalidate/refetch the connectedCalendars query, the 'Cache Status'/'Last updated' timestamp shown in the dropdown remains stale after a successful cache deletion.
raw_findings.root_cause: deleteCache mutation's onSuccess handler omits invalidation/refetch of the connectedCalendars query cache that supplies cacheUpdatedAt
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in an onSettled/onSuccess handler of deleteCacheMutation, mirroring the pattern used in disconnectMutation.
raw_findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars cache after success
raw_findings.trigger: User deletes calendar cache via the dropdown; the sibling disconnectMutation explicitly invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in its onSettled, but deleteCacheMutation relies solely on the caller-supplied onSuccess callback.

validated_findings.body: tRPC surfaces this as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) rather than a proper NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN error code, which breaks correct client-side error handling/monitoring and misclassifies an expected authorization failure as a server bug.
validated_findings.evidence: throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied");
validated_findings.failure_mode: tRPC wraps unclassified errors as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, obscuring the real cause
validated_findings.impact: tRPC surfaces this as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) rather than a proper NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN error code, which breaks correct client-side error handling/monitoring and misclassifies an expected authorization failure as a server bug.
validated_findings.root_cause: Handler throws a plain JS Error instead of a TRPCError with an appropriate error code
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Throw a `TRPCError` from `@trpc/server` with an appropriate code (e.g. `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`) instead of a plain `Error`.
validated_findings.title: deleteCacheHandler throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
validated_findings.trigger: A user attempts to delete cache for a credentialId they do not own (e.g. tampered request, stale UI state, or race with credential deletion), causing `credential` to be null.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 25 exists verbatim with `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC, throwing a plain Error instead of TRPCError results in INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR being surfaced to clients. The trigger (user attempts to delete cache for non-owned credential) is realistic, and the impact (opaque 500 instead of proper NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) follows from tRPC's error handling behavior.

validated_findings.body: If the parent's onSuccess callback does not itself invalidate/refetch the connectedCalendars query, the 'Cache Status'/'Last updated' timestamp shown in the dropdown remains stale after a successful cache deletion.
validated_findings.failure_mode: UI continues to display the pre-deletion cache timestamp until an unrelated refetch occurs
validated_findings.impact: If the parent's onSuccess callback does not itself invalidate/refetch the connectedCalendars query, the 'Cache Status'/'Last updated' timestamp shown in the dropdown remains stale after a successful cache deletion.
validated_findings.root_cause: deleteCache mutation's onSuccess handler omits invalidation/refetch of the connectedCalendars query cache that supplies cacheUpdatedAt
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in an onSettled/onSuccess handler of deleteCacheMutation, mirroring the pattern used in disconnectMutation.
validated_findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars cache after success
validated_findings.trigger: User deletes calendar cache via the dropdown; the sibling disconnectMutation explicitly invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in its onSettled, but deleteCacheMutation relies solely on the caller-supplied onSuccess callback.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that cache invalidation is missing is speculative. The code shows `onSuccess?.()` is called, delegating to the parent's callback. Without evidence that the parent fails to invalidate, this is an ungrounded assumption about caller behavior. The finding assumes the parent's onSuccess doesn't invalidate, but that's not proven by the patch.

validated_findings.body: The script may fail outright without network access, or behave inconsistently across machines due to an unpinned tsx version, unlike the previous `ts-node` invocation which relied on a project-local dependency.
validated_findings.failure_mode: npx fetches/resolves tsx at runtime, causing failures offline or version drift across environments
validated_findings.impact: The script may fail outright without network access, or behave inconsistently across machines due to an unpinned tsx version, unlike the previous `ts-node` invocation which relied on a project-local dependency.
validated_findings.root_cause: Script command switched to invoke 'npx tsx' without adding tsx as a pinned devDependency
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add `tsx` as a pinned devDependency and invoke it directly (e.g. `tsx cron-tester.ts`) instead of `npx tsx`.
validated_findings.title: dev:cron script switched to npx tsx without pinning dependency
validated_findings.trigger: A developer or CI runner without `tsx` already cached/installed executes `yarn dev:cron` in an offline or network-restricted environment, or on a machine with a different globally-resolved tsx version.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about npx tsx causing offline failures or version drift is speculative. npx caches packages locally after first use, and this is a dev script not production code. The impact is minor and the trigger (offline CI/dev environment) is not a realistic production concern for a dev:cron script.

validated_findings.body: The purely informational status row is focusable/selectable like an action item, so activating it triggers an unintended onSelect (closing the menu) and misleads assistive technology into treating static text as an actionable control.
validated_findings.evidence:
{t("cache_status")}
{t("cache_last_updated", { timestamp: new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short", }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)), interpolation: { escapeValue: false }, })}
validated_findings.failure_mode: Keyboard/screen-reader users can select/activate the status row causing an unintended onSelect trigger and menu close, and assistive tech announces it as an actionable item though it does nothing
validated_findings.impact: The purely informational status row is focusable/selectable like an action item, so activating it triggers an unintended onSelect (closing the menu) and misleads assistive technology into treating static text as an actionable control.
validated_findings.root_cause: Static, non-interactive cache status text is wrapped in an interactive DropdownMenuItem instead of a non-interactive label element
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Render the cache status block with a non-interactive element (e.g. a DropdownMenuLabel or a plain div outside DropdownMenuItem) instead of DropdownMenuItem.
validated_findings.title: Static cache status wrapped in interactive DropdownMenuItem
validated_findings.trigger: A keyboard or screen-reader user navigates the dropdown menu to the non-actionable 'Cache Status' row and presses Enter/Space, or the assistive tech announces it as a selectable action.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 84 exists verbatim showing static cache status text wrapped in DropdownMenuItem. DropdownMenuItem is typically an interactive element that receives focus and triggers onSelect. Using it for purely informational content is an accessibility issue - keyboard users can select it expecting an action. The trigger and impact are realistic.
